description: Decide what an arriving worker-lifecycle message does. A run the orchestrator terminated and replaced keeps sending, and it sends for an issue that has a running entry - the new one. A message is accounted only when its run_id equals the run_id of the issue's current running entry; otherwise it is discarded and that entry and its worker are left in place. Testing only whether a running entry is present is not sufficient, because after a reconciliation-initiated termination and a re-dispatch the entry a stale message must not consume is present by construction.
given: { entry: { run_id: string } | null, exit_run_id: string }
notes: The file mirrors retry-fire-disposition.json's one-shot pure-function shape: one arriving message, one entry, one decision. Nothing here is a live invocation.

The rule is stated over the worker-orchestrator channel rather than over the exit alone (Section 8.5), so the same three cases decide an agent update. An agent update writes last_timestamp, which is Part A's own stall reference (Section 16.3); the disposition is what keeps a dead run's trailing events from holding a stalled replacement alive. account means the message is accounted to that entry - for an exit, removing it and taking the retry decision; for an update, writing the live-session fields.

entry_retained on the stale case is the assertion a remove-first implementation fails: it takes the entry before it compares, so the live run's entry is gone and its worker is left with nothing tracking it.
run_id values are opaque strings here. SPEC.md Section 4.1.5 leaves the derivation Implementation-defined and fixes only the distinction the value makes, so no vector depends on a format.

vectors.description: The live run's own message. It is accounted and, for an exit, the entry is consumed.
A run reconciliation terminated has been replaced by a re-dispatch, and the terminated run's message arrives afterwards. It is discarded, and the live entry and its worker stand untouched.

A message for an issue that has no running entry - the case Section 8.5 already stated, now the case where there is nothing to match rather than a rule of its own. Reached whenever reconciliation terminated the run and nothing has been dispatched since.
